title: The Six Ancestral Roads
subtitle: A long branch from the Maynard home: six destinations across two continents, every scene anchored to signed records. Imagined material is always labelled.

destinations.name: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania
destinations.blurb: The McCabe-McAvoy road: Scotland and Ireland to Allegheny County.

destinations.name: Butler County, Pennsylvania
destinations.blurb: The Elliott-McQuiston road: Center Township and New Castle, Pennsylvania.

destinations.name: San Diego, California
destinations.blurb: The Smith-Bowman-Prickett road: Illinois to Colorado, Indiana to Greeley to San Diego.

destinations.name: Floyd County, Iowa
destinations.blurb: The Shapley-Schlorff road: New York and Michigan roots, Iowa, Chicago, Pasco and Minneapolis.

destinations.name: Dassel, Minnesota
destinations.blurb: The Maynard-Hillman road: Kentucky to Meeker County, on to Florida and California.

destinations.name: Paleschken, West Prussia
destinations.blurb: The Hedtke-Luedtke road: Kreis Berent to Sibley County, Minnesota, to Fresno.

scenes.title: The Six Ancestral Roads
scenes.fact: Every family in the signed tree arrived somewhere. This branch follows six roads out of the Maynard home: Pittsburgh, Butler County, San Diego, Floyd County Iowa, Dassel Minnesota, and Paleschken in West Prussia.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined scene-setting) Six wagon roads leave the same farmyard at dawn. The names on the signposts are all in the signed records.
scenes.tag: Branch structure grounded in signed-records-20261121-075603-743.json.
scenes.discovery: Six destinations are available from the road map.

scenes.title: Pick your first road
scenes.fact: The destinations correspond to recorded life places of named ancestors in the signed tree.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) Dust, a compass, and six hand-painted signs.
scenes.tag: Signed records; see facts list at the end of the branch.
scenes.discovery: The map scene itself is a hub: all six roads and the activity deck are reachable from here.

scenes.title: Scotland to Allegheny County
scenes.fact: Edward Mccabe [TG307645] was born in March 1861 in Scotland. His parents were James McCabe [TG654147], born about 1840 in Ireland, and Mary [TG812186], born about 1844 in Ireland. The 1900 U.S. Census places an Edward McCabe in Pittsburgh Ward 35, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A ship's manifest chalked on a dock board: Glasgow to the Allegheny.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG307645, TG654147, TG812186; WikiTree Mccabe-2780 (1900 census, Pittsburgh Ward 35). Tentative: exact death year (signed record says 1900 PA; the 1900 census shows him alive in June 1900).
scenes.discovery: The McCabe line left Ireland and Scotland for Pittsburgh's steel towns.

scenes.title: Cockermouth and the McAvoy line
scenes.fact: Sarah McAvoy [TG918273] was born 13 April 1862 in Derwent Street, Cockermouth, Cumberland, England, and died in 1934 in Pennsylvania. Her parents were James McAvoy [TG891052], born 17 March 1833 in Ireland and died 24 October 1906 in Scott, Allegheny County, PA, and Rosamund Sloan [TG540918], born 1838 in Ireland and died 10 November 1912 in Scott, Allegheny County, PA.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) Two rivers: the Derwent in Cumberland and the Allegheny in Pittsburgh, drawn on one map.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG918273, TG891052, TG540918. Tentative: one secondary source gives Sarah's birthplace as Ireland and her birth year as about 1863 (WikiTree Mc_Avoy-353); the signed record says Cockermouth, England, 1862.
scenes.discovery: Sarah McAvoy married Edward Mccabe; both families landed in the same Scott/Allegheny area of Pennsylvania.

scenes.title: County Down roots
scenes.fact: Sarah's maternal grandparents were John Sloan, born May 1820 in County Down, Ireland, died 1 August 1900 in Washington Township, Cambria County, PA, and Ann McGowan, born about 1822 in County Down, Ireland. Her paternal grandparents were Patrick McAvoy, born about 1797 in Ireland, and Mary Evett, born about 1797 in Newry, Ireland.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A letter in two hands, Ulster and Cumberland, addressed to one Pittsburgh address.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records (persons 68-71: Patrick McAvoy, Mary Evett, John Sloan, Ann McGowan).
scenes.discovery: The McAvoy and Sloan families both trace to County Down, Ireland, before Pennsylvania.

scenes.title: John McCabe, 1896
scenes.fact: John McCabe [TG628417], son of Edward Mccabe and Sarah McAvoy, was born 9 February 1896 in Allegheny County, Pittsburgh, PA, and died in August 1982 at Chestnut Ridge Cemetery, Eldersville, Washington County, Pennsylvania.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A February snow on the Monongahela, and a birth registered that week.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed record TG628417.
scenes.discovery: John McCabe's 1896 Pittsburgh birth connects the McCabe-McAvoy marriage to the next generation in Pennsylvania.

scenes.title: Somerset County, 1817
scenes.fact: James Elliott [TG673245, TG749502] was born in April 1817 in Somerset County, Pennsylvania, and died in 1906 in Butler County, Pennsylvania. His parents were John Elliott and Margaret Scott [TG771250], born 10 February 1793 in Mercer, Franklin County, PA, died 1 April 1868 in Butler, Butler County, PA.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A farm on the Conemaugh, counted in the 1820 census.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG673245/TG749502, TG771250, person 129 (John Elliott). Note: TG673245 is marked non-permanent in the registry.
scenes.discovery: James Elliott moved his family from Somerset County to Butler County, Pennsylvania.

scenes.title: James N Elliott, Center Township
scenes.fact: James N Elliott [TG654890], son of James Elliott and Margaret Elliott [TG182976], was born 12 October 1855 in Center Township, Butler County, PA, and died 1 November 1926 in Center, Butler, Pennsylvania. He married Elizabeth McQuiston [TG270541].
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) October frost on the Center Township fields.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed record TG654890; Find a Grave memorial 222439556 and an Ancestry record corroborate the name and dates.
scenes.discovery: James N Elliott's Center Township dates (1855-1926) anchor the Elliott line in Butler County.

scenes.title: The McQuiston family
scenes.fact: Elizabeth McQuiston [TG270541] was born 7 January 1887 in Pennsylvania and died 27 August 1940 in New Castle, Lawrence County, PA. Her parents were Charles McQuiston [TG804631], born 25 March 1850 in Butler County, PA, died 31 July 1917 in Butler, PA, and Mary Thorpe [TG295740], born 27 January 1863 in Pennsylvania, died 30 May 1944 in New Castle, Lawrence County, PA. Charles's parents were Marshall McQuiston, born 23 November 1813 in Butler, PA, died 22 December 1872 in Butler County, and Rebecca Grannis, born 26 March 1819 in Massachusetts, died 31 October 1905 near Slippery Rock, Butler County, PA.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A family Bible with the McQuiston name spelled three ways.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG270541, TG804631, TG295740, persons 76-77. Context: Mitchell (1937), The McQuiston, McCuiston and McQuesten Families, 1620-1937; gmccuistion.com.
scenes.discovery: The McQuiston line has been documented since 1620; Mitchell's 1937 family history is the standard reference.

scenes.title: New Castle, 1906-1951
scenes.fact: Alice S Elliott [TG492705], daughter of James N Elliott and Elizabeth McQuiston, was born 12 June 1906 in Butler, PA, and died 24 December 1951 in New Castle, Pennsylvania.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A Christmas Eve death registered in New Castle, 1951.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed record TG492705; WikiTree profile Elliott-15069 corroborates.

choices.label: Talk to a Butler County local (imagined)

scenes.discovery: Alice S Elliott's 1906 Butler birth and 1951 New Castle death close the Elliott-McQuiston road.

scenes.title: Mattoon and Braceville, 1862-1869
scenes.fact: Albert Franklin Smith [TG839162] was born 15 March 1862 in Mattoon, Coles County, Illinois, and died 20 December 1946 at Fairlawn Burial Park, Hutchinson, Reno County, Kansas. He married Rose Ann Prickett [TG501784], born 30 July 1869 in Braceville, Grundy County, Illinois, died 28 October 1952 in Yuma, Yuma County, Colorado.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A railroad timetable for the Wabash out of Mattoon.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG839162, TG501784; Find a Grave memorial 10143299 for Albert Franklin Smith.
scenes.discovery: Albert Franklin Smith and Rose Ann Prickett were both born in Illinois in the 1860s.

scenes.title: Pittsburgh to Yuma: the grandparents
scenes.fact: Albert's parents were John Isaac Smith, born 18 February 1821 in Pittsburgh, Allegheny County, PA, died 7 December 1916 in Wray, Yuma County, Colorado, and Ruanna Hamilton, born 27 July 1827 in Gnadenhutten, Tuscarawas County, Ohio, died 19 February 1908 in Monegaw Springs, St. Clair County, Missouri. Rose Ann's parents were Charles Prickett, born 16 October 1829 in Apakesha Grove, Champaign County, Ohio, died 10 July 1903 in Vernon, Yuma County, Colorado, and Adaline A Holderman, born 24 April 1835 in Marion County, Ohio, died 28 September 1918 in Yuma County, Colorado.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) Two covered wagons crossing at a Yuma County crossroads.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records persons 40-43 (John Isaac Smith, Ruanna Hamilton, Charles Prickett, Adaline A Holderman).
scenes.discovery: Both sides of the Smith-Prickett marriage ended up in Yuma County, Colorado.

scenes.title: Archie T Smith and Myrtle Bowman
scenes.fact: Archie T Smith [TG713289], son of Albert Franklin Smith and Rose Ann Prickett, was born 21 September 1894 in Greeley, Weld County, Colorado, and died 8 May 1973 in San Diego, San Diego County, California. He married Polly Myrtle Bowman [TG856134], born 18 May 1887 in Morgan County, Indiana, died 24 June 1955 in San Diego, California.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A wedding in a Greeley church, 1910s; a drive west to San Diego later.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG713289, TG856134; Smith Official DNA Project tree entry (Greeley CO, d. 8 May 1973 San Diego); Ancestry public-tree record for Polly Myrtle Bowman (b. 18 May 1887 Morgan, IN; parents Thomas S Bowman, Nancy Jane Lambert); Find a Grave memorials 224035291 and 255313550.
scenes.discovery: Archie T Smith's Greeley birth and San Diego death were confirmed by the Smith DNA project tree.

scenes.title: Morgan County, Indiana and the next generation
scenes.fact: Polly Myrtle Bowman's parents were Thomas S Bowman [TG962430], born February 1863 in Eminence, Morgan County, Indiana, died 1904, and Nancy Jane Lambert [TG348671], born 8 June 1864 in Morgan County, Indiana, died 5 November 1946 in Jefferson County, Indiana. Nancy's parents were Aaron Lorenzo Lambert [TG684510], born 13 October 1830 in Randolph, North Carolina, died 19 January 1910 in Morgan, Indiana, and Tabitha Ann Brown, born 10 August 1838 in Hall, Morgan County, Indiana, died 27 April 1915. Aaron's parents were Henry Ira Lambert, born 24 May 1796 in North Carolina, died 1868 in Hendricks County, Indiana, and Sarah 'Sally' M Craven, born 1809 in Randolph, North Carolina, died 27 January 1887 in Center Valley, Indiana. Archie and Myrtle's daughter was Noma Vade Smith [TG315902], born 19 March 1927 in San Diego, California, died 20 December 1991 in San Diego County, California.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) Sorghum fields in Morgan County, and later, Pacific air in San Diego.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG962430, TG348671, TG684510, TG315902, persons 44-45, 47, 92-93; Find a Grave memorial 10806355 for Aaron Lorenzo Lambert.

choices.label: Talk to a San Diego local (imagined)

scenes.discovery: The Bowman-Lambert line runs from North Carolina through Indiana to San Diego.

scenes.title: New York and Michigan roots
scenes.fact: Percy W Shapley [TG739123] was born 6 May 1901 in Floyd, Floyd County, Iowa, and died 11 September 1946 in Pasco, Franklin County, Washington. His father was William Shapley, born about 1798/1799 in Granville, Washington County, New York, died between 1861 and 1864 in Iowa, with Mary Rice, born February 1849 in Wisconsin. William's father was Patrick Henry Shapley, born 10 April 1846 in Emmett, Calhoun County, Michigan, with Clarissa Gridley, born about 1804 in New York.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A sod house on the Floyd County prairie, 1901.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed record TG739123 (death 11 Sep 1946 Pasco, Franklin Co. WA). Tentative: birth (signed record 6 May 1901 Floyd, IA; WikiTree Shapley line says 1 Jan 1902 Iowa).

choices.label: The Stafford side of Floyd County

scenes.discovery: The Shapley line reaches back to Granville, New York, and Emmett, Michigan.

scenes.title: Calamus and Charles City
scenes.fact: Percy's mother was Olive G Stafford [TG759401], born 30 April 1876 in Calamus, Dodge County... recorded as Calamus, Wisconsin, died 22 May 1946 in Charles City, Floyd County, Iowa. Her parents included Joseph W Stafford, born 1804 in New York, and Hulda Sylvah, born 1811 in Pennsylvania, died 1862 in Wisconsin; and Barton J Waite, born 1792 in New York, died 1862/1870 in Calamus, Dodge County, Wisconsin, with Susannah Clark Bacon, born 20 August 1790 in Randolph, Orange County, Vermont, died December 1870 in Lorain, Lorain County, Ohio. Alice Waite, born 27 November 1840 in Lorain, Lorain County, Ohio, died 4 July 1914 in Gardena, Bottineau County, North Dakota.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) The Cedar River at Charles City, where the Staffords settled.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG759401, persons 58-59, 113, 116-119.
scenes.discovery: The Stafford and Waite lines crossed from New York and Vermont through Wisconsin to Floyd County, Iowa.

scenes.title: Minnie Schlorff, Chicago 1905
scenes.fact: Minnie Schlorff [TG742018] was born 1 March 1905 at 10920 Mackinaw Avenue, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois, and died 12 April 1946 in Minneapolis, Hennepin County, Minnesota. Her parents were William John Ludwig Sclorf [TG916000], born 21 July 1867 in Pomerania, Prussia, died 1937 in Wisconsin, and Mary Johannsen [TG324786], born 28 November 1868 in Tondern, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, died 1951 in Shawano County, Wisconsin. She married Percy W Shapley in 1924.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A 1924 wedding license filed in Iowa, a Chicago address on the certificate.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG742018, TG916000, TG324786; Geneanet family tree (m. Percy W Shapley 1924); Reddit r/Genealogy and MyHeritage name records (b. 1 Mar 1905 Chicago, d. 12 Apr 1946 Minneapolis); Find a Grave memorial 239646934 (Minnie Schlorff Andrews). Tentative: later marriage to Leland J Andrews (1943) appears only in user-submitted sources.
scenes.discovery: Minnie Schlorff's Chicago birth and Minneapolis death are corroborated by multiple independent name-record sources.

scenes.title: Pasco and Minneapolis, 1946
scenes.fact: Percy W Shapley died 11 September 1946 in Pasco, Franklin County, Washington, and Minnie Schlorff died 12 April 1946 in Minneapolis, Hennepin County, Minnesota — the two ends of the Shapley-Schlorff road in 1946.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) Two towns, one spring, 1946: the Columbia River at Pasco, the Mississippi at Minneapolis.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG739123, TG742018; WikiTree Shapley line (d. 11 Sep 1946 Pasco, Franklin, WA).
scenes.discovery: Both Percy Shapley and Minnie Schlorff died in 1946, months apart, in Washington and Minnesota.

scenes.title: Kentucky to Dassel
scenes.fact: William R Maynard [TG715094] was born 13 December 1878 in Dassel, Meeker County, Minnesota, and died 24 November 1958 in Brooksville, Hernando County, Florida. His father was George Maynard [TG859743], born 27 August 1852 in Prestonsburg, Floyd County, Kentucky, died 2 May 1932 in Minot, Ward County, North Dakota. His mother was Margaret Rose Sansom [TG502168], born 11 February 1859 in Logan County, Kentucky, died 28 December 1928 in Rosehill, Covington, Alabama.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A December birth in a Meeker County farmhouse, 1878.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG715094, TG859743, TG502168; Coastal Breeze News confirms William R Maynard's later life in Brooksville, FL; WikiTree Maynard-103 (George Maynard).
scenes.discovery: William R Maynard's parents both came from Kentucky — George from Floyd County, Margaret from Logan County.

scenes.title: Pike County, Kentucky roots
scenes.fact: George Maynard's parents were William Maynard, born 18 May 1830 in Pike County, Kentucky, died 25 March 1908 in Pierce County, Washington, and Sarah Parsons, born 9 August 1821 in Kentucky, died 14 March 1891 in Bertha, Todd County, Minnesota. The 1870 census shows William Maynard, age 40, a farmer and township supervisor in Dassel Township, Meeker County, Minnesota, living at Swan Lake with his wife Sarah, age 42. Margaret Rose Sansom's parents were Riley Sansom, born 10 February 1831 in Pike County, Kentucky, died 6 April 1905 in Riverside, Snohomish County, Washington, and Sarah Sally Kline, born 20 July 1836 in Glen Alum, Logan County, Virginia/West Virginia, died 6 September 1928 in Snohomish, Snohomish County, Washington.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A township supervisor's ledger in Dassel, 1870.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records persons 96-99; WikiTree Maynard-162 (1870 census, Dassel Township, Meeker Co. MN; Find a Grave 158111098, Sumner Cemetery, Pierce Co. WA).
scenes.discovery: William Maynard Sr. was already a Dassel Township supervisor by 1870 — the family was rooted in Meeker County.

scenes.title: Gail Agnes Hillman of Cannon Falls
scenes.fact: Gail Agnes Hillman [TG286753], William R Maynard's wife, was born 21 September 1884 in Cannon Falls, Goodhue County, Minnesota, and died 12 April 1982 in Saint Paul, Ramsey County, Minnesota. Her parents were Fred Ernest Hillman [TG796320], born 21 August 1857 in Minnesota, died 4 December 1950 at Bald Eagle Center, Cass County, Minnesota, and Agnes Maria Platt [TG148675], born 27 April 1857 in Palmyra, Jefferson County, Wisconsin, died 23 February 1946 in Ramsey County, Minnesota.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) The Cannon River at Cannon Falls, 1884.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG286753, TG796320, TG148675.
scenes.discovery: Gail Agnes Hillman was born in Cannon Falls, Goodhue County, and died in Saint Paul, both in Minnesota.

scenes.title: Massachusetts to Cannon Falls; North Dakota to Morro Bay
scenes.fact: Fred Ernest Hillman's parents were Levi Colburn Hillman, born 25 January 1822 in Conway, Franklin County, Massachusetts, died 11 March 1861 in Randolph, Dakota Territory (Minnesota), and Mary Marinda Shelly, born 1830 in Connecticut, died 11 March 1897 in Randolph, Dakota County, MN. Agnes Maria Platt's parents were David C Platt [TG158342], born 16 May 1823 in Berne, Clinton County, New York, died 23 October 1904 in Cannon Falls, Goodhue County, MN, and Miranda McLane, born 12 March 1817 in Alburgh, Grand Isle County, Vermont, died 24 July 1861 in Werner, Juneau County, Wisconsin. William R Maynard and Gail Agnes Hillman's son was Burke C Maynard [TG239670], born 11 June 1904 in North Dakota, died 5 December 1986 in Morro Bay, San Luis Obispo County, California.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) From a Massachusetts hill farm to a Cannon Falls parlor; from Minot, North Dakota to the Morro Bay coast.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG239670, TG158342, persons 100-103; Find a Grave memorial 93464196 (Burke C Maynard); Find a Grave 81879786 (David C Platt); Find a Grave 91939608 (Fred Ernest Hillman); Find a Grave 87752705 (Agnes Maria Hillman).
scenes.discovery: The Maynard-Hillman road runs Massachusetts -> Minnesota -> North Dakota -> Florida and California.

scenes.title: Paleschken, Kreis Berent, 1847
scenes.fact: August Friedrich Hedtke [TG923450] was born 23 August 1847 in Alt Paleschken, Kreis Berent, Regierungsbezirk Danzig, West Prussia, and died 31 January 1918 in Henderson, Sibley County, Minnesota. He married Amelia Carolina Luedtke [TG610982], born February 1850 in Pomerania, Prussia, died 24 April 1925 in Henderson, Sibley County, Minnesota.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A West Prussian village church register, 1847.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG923450, TG610982; Find a Grave memorial 75234154 (August F. Hedtke).
scenes.discovery: August Friedrich Hedtke and Amelia Carolina Luedtke both died in Henderson, Sibley County, Minnesota.

scenes.title: Johann and Florentine Hedtke
scenes.fact: August Friedrich Hedtke's parents were Johann E Hedtke [TG842378], born 5 December 1819 in West Prussia, died 28 August 1894 in Chaska, Carver County, Minnesota, and Florentine Henriette Florence Hedtke [TG413360], born 31 July 1828 in Neu or Alt Paleschken, Berent, Danzig, West Prussia, died 18 February 1901 in Chaska, Carver County, Minnesota.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) Two Paleschken graves, and later two Chaska churchyard stones.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG842378, TG413360; Find a Grave memorial 54692058.
scenes.discovery: The Hedtke line moved from Paleschken (West Prussia) to Chaska (Carver County, Minnesota).

scenes.title: Robert R Hedtke, Sibley, Minnesota
scenes.fact: Robert R Hedtke [TG903148], son of August Friedrich Hedtke and Amelia Carolina Luedtke, was born 18 January 1876 in Sibley, Minnesota, and died 13 February 1954 in Fresno, California. He married Amelia Kiehlbauch [TG472690], the link back to the Kiehlbauch-Beck branch.
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A January birth on the Minnesota prairie, 1876.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed record TG903148 (death 13 Feb 1954 Fresno, CA; Find a Grave 260875592). Tentative: birth month (signed record 18 Jan 1876; a FamilySearch-derived tree says June 1876, Sibley County, MN).
scenes.discovery: Robert R Hedtke's Fresno death (13 Feb 1954) matches across the signed record and the FamilySearch-derived tree.

scenes.title: Amelia B Hetdke and the link to Fresno
scenes.fact: Robert R Hedtke and Amelia Kiehlbauch's daughter was Amelia B Hetdke [TG984215], born 28 December 1904 in North Dakota, died 15 May 1979 in Morro Bay, San Luis Obispo County, California. Through Amelia Kiehlbauch, this road joins the Maynard home via Burke C Maynard [TG239670].
scenes.fiction: (Imagined) A family photograph album passed from Tyndall to Fresno to Morro Bay.
scenes.tag: Verified: signed records TG984215, TG472690, TG239670.
scenes.discovery: Amelia B Hetdke (1904 North Dakota - 1979 Morro Bay) is the Hedtke-Maynard link in this generation.

activities.title: Route the emigrants
activities.instructions: Which route did Black Sea German families such as the Kiehlbauchs generally take to South Dakota?
activities.question: Best-supported route from the Odessa colonies to Tyndall, SD:
options: Odessa -> steamship via Bremen/Hamburg -> New York -> rail west via Chicago -> Dakota Territory
Odessa -> overland wagon straight across Canada
Odessa -> Ellis Island -> direct steamer to San Francisco -> wagon east
Odessa -> London -> Halifax -> Montreal -> wagon south
activities.explain: FamilySearch and the AHSGR passenger-list guides document Bremen/Hamburg departures and rail travel west; the SD Historical Society 1909 report describes arrivals via rail to Yankton. Exact ship/manifest for this family: not found.

activities.title: Sort the sources
activities.question: Which of these is the strongest evidence for a birth date in this branch?
options: A signed HVZA record with a permanent TG identifier
A user-submitted Find a Grave memorial alone
An imagined scene in this game
activities.explain: Signed records with permanent TG codes are the project's primary layer; Wikipedia and user memorials are contextual or tentative; game scenes labelled imagined are fiction.

exchanges.them: Joseph Kiehlbauch's family ran the farm outside town — he himself died in Chicago in 1908.
Barbara Beck is buried here — died 1923. Her father Constantin died out in Lustdorf before the crossing.
Amelia Kiehlbauch, born here in 1880, married Burke Maynard. Their daughter Amelia went to North Dakota, then California.

activities.title: The Record Room (mini text adventure)
activities.instructions: Type commands like: look, take card, read card, decode word, unlock drawer, open drawer. Original puzzle inspired by reading themes (spy kits, code words, ordered puzzles, verb-noun text adventures) from Sufficiently Educated via TextWarden read-only search; no book text or Zork assets reproduced.
activities.intro: You are in the family record room. A locked drawer holds a record card. On the desk: an inkwell, a cipher card, and a brass key.

steps.resp: Desk: inkwell, cipher card, brass key. Locked drawer. Door east to the hall.
You take the cipher card. It reads: SHIW WKH UHFRUG LV LQ WKH GUDZHU. Clue below: shift each letter back by 3.
SHIW WKH UHFRUG LV LQ WKH GUDZHU. (Caesar shift -3)
Shifting each letter back by 3 gives: 'THE RECORD IS IN THE DRAWER.' The code word is RECORD.
The brass key turns. The drawer unlocks. (You needed the code word first: try 'decode word' before 'unlock drawer'.)
Inside: a record card for Amelia Kiehlbauch [TG472690], b. 12 Jan 1880 Tyndall, Bon Homme Co., SD; d. 29 Aug 1969 Fresno, CA - verified signed record. Puzzle complete.

activities.win: Drawer open. Verified record retrieved: Amelia Kiehlbauch [TG472690].
